title: Bloomberg US Aggregate Index rebalance takes effect at the month-end close — the booking date for a composition change already fixed earlier in the month
source: EST: owner-published, from two Bloomberg documents fetched direct 2026-09-09 and text-extracted in-session. (1) Bloomberg US Aggregate Index factsheet, June 12 2024 (assets.bbhub.io/professional/sites/27/US-Aggregate-Index.pdf, HTTP 200, 141,886 bytes, 16 content streams inflated), whose index-parameters block states verbatim: 'Rebalance Date — The last business day of each month.' (2) Bloomberg Fixed Income Index Methodology, October 15 2024 (assets.bbhub.io/professional/sites/27/Fixed-Income-Index-Methodology.pdf, HTTP 200, 1,795,685 bytes, 456 streams inflated) — the governing document the factsheet says it 'is intended to be read in conjunction with' — which gives the same rule as a standing mechanic: 'At the close of the last business day of each month, the Bloomberg Indices are reset and bonds formally enter and exit the index.' The last business day of September 2026 is Wednesday 2026-09-30, reproduced independently by weekday arithmetic against the tracked labor-day-market-closure-2026-09-07 entry (first Monday 09-07; no further US market holiday falls in September 2026) and cross-checked against home.treasury.gov's own daily yield-curve series, which publishes a row for every US bond-market session. Filed estimate on the two standing counts every index-flow entry on this calendar documents: the confirmed-prefix taxonomy in market-events-data.ts has IR:/CAL:/BLS:/FED:/TSY: and no member for an INDEX OWNER'S own published methodology — the same gap sp-select-sector-secondary-reweight-2026-09-30 and every Russell entry name — and this lane does not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep. The DATE RULE IS THE OWNER'S OWN and is not in doubt; the estimate label is about the taxonomy, not the evidence
notes: THE REBALANCE DATE IS A BOOKING DATE, NOT AN INFORMATION DATE — and that is the correction this entry exists to carry. The proposal that filed this id (from-treasury-5y-note-2026-09-23) built its case on settlement: the 2Y/5Y/7Y auctioned 09-22/23/24 settle 2026-09-30, 'so the new issue enters the index universe at the rebalance.' The owner's methodology refutes the mechanism in one sentence: 'Qualifying securities issued but NOT NECESSARILY SETTLED on or before the month-end rebalancing date will qualify for inclusion in the following month's index,' and, for Treasuries specifically, 'US Treasuries are added to the Projected Universes of the US Aggregate and US Treasury Indices with an assumed coupon ON THE ANNOUNCEMENT DATE, if auctioned in the same month.' Settlement is explicitly irrelevant; the coupons would enter this rebalance settling in October. The settlement/rebalance coincidence is a coincidence, not a channel. TWO SECURITIES THE PROPOSAL COUNTED ARE NOT INDEX-ELIGIBLE AT ALL: the factsheet's Excluded list names 'Inflation-linked bonds, floating-rate issues', so the 2Y FRN (09-23) and the 10Y TIPS (09-17) never enter the US Aggregate. THE DATES THAT DO CARRY INFORMATION, all earlier than 09-30: the announcement date of each auction (treasury.gov's own auctions_query, fetched direct 2026-09-09, shows the September refunding block — 3Y $58bn, 10Y reopening $39bn, 30Y reopening $22bn, $119bn of index-eligible fixed-rate coupon supply — was ANNOUNCED 2026-09-03 and had entered the Projected Universe six days before this entry was written); the 2026-09-17 coupon announcement (already tracked) for the 2Y/5Y/7Y; and T-3 = Friday 2026-09-25, the factsheet's cut-off for SOMA float adjustments to Treasury amount outstanding, after which they are held constant into month-end. IMPACT LOW, and the ledger measures why rather than asserting it: over 3,920 sessions of FRED DGS10 (2011-01-03 to 2026-09-04) the last business day of the month averages -0.88bp in 10Y yield (t=-2.62) and the last three sessions -2.29bp (t=-4.11) against a +0.11bp all-window baseline — but QUARTER-END month-ends average +0.11bp (t=0.23, no effect), September month-ends +0.87bp with 5 of 15 lower, and the run-in effect decays to -1.60bp (t=-1.54) in 2021-2026. The proposal's 'September is a quarter-end, when the extension is customarily largest' is not visible in the tape. SYMBOLS DELIBERATELY EMPTY: the flow lives in the Treasury curve, and an AGG/BND proxy would only make the deterministic screen fire on broad rate beta rather than on anything about this event; a 5% move in AGG is a historic rates event, not a rebalance. KIND 'sector' matches the sibling index-flow entries; the enum has no index-flow member and the imperfect fit is named here rather than fixed from this lane. Any ledger citing this entry carries the estimate label and treats it as a reason to widen caution about month-end execution, never as a licence to act.
